title: Seller Proving Ground: Rapid Heuristics & Simulation Notes (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a hands-on ‘Proving Ground’ that lets seller/SE pairs run rapid tabletop simulations (3–12 minute scenarios) to internalize fallback heuristics and tradeoff language for inference projects. Goal is to produce repeatable micro-scripts, a short rubric for success, and a small pilot to run with 12 field reps next quarter.

What this doc is NOT:
- Final slide deck. More of a facilitator notebook + scenario bank.
- Comprehensive pricing/legal guidance — link to procurement deck for that.

Core constraints we teach (one-liners for reps):
- When latency matters, prefer pinned dedicated model endpoints + aggressive prefix caching.
- When cost rules, prefer quantized variants + batching and short-sequence prompts.
- When data controls matter, escalate to Private (VPC) + KMS and call SRE.
- Default fallback: route to verified smaller model with preserved prompt form.

Format for each micro-scenario (3-step):
1) Setup (customer, persona, signal that triggers escalation)
2) Ask the rep must make (primary decision and one fallback)
3) Acceptance criteria and one-line seller script

Scenario bank (compact):
- Scenario A — eCommerce personalization, low latency SLA (target <150ms p95):
  Setup: Head of Product for mobile checkout. They complain about checkout drop when recommendations delay.
  Decision: Recommend Dedicated capacity + KV prefix caching for recommendations or propose sampling fewer features.
  Script: "If checkout impact is on the critical path, we recommend a reserved endpoint tuned for short sequences — keeps p95 under target and gives predictable cost; we can pilot a small pool for 2 weeks and measure checkout lift."
  Acceptance: Pilot with 5000 daily requests keeps p95 < 150ms and error rate <1%.

- Scenario B — Fintech docs ingestion, data sovereignty requirement:
  Setup: Security lead insists on no PII leaving VPC.
  Decision: Propose Redwood Private (VPC) with customer-managed keys + audit logs; if on-prem required, start with small air-gapped package.
  Script: "We’ll scope a Private deployment with KMS integration and a 30-day audit window — team will provide a minimal network diagram and we’ll produce a security checklist for procurement."
  Acceptance: Legal signs NDA + SOC mapping, signoff on network diagram within 3 sprints.

- Scenario C — Startup with cost ceilings, wants embeddings at scale:
  Setup: Growth PM wants embeddings for search but can’t exceed $X/month.
  Decision: Recommend batched embedding jobs + incremental caching + cheaper quantized embedder; offer Optimize session for configuration.
  Script: "We can lower unit cost by batching and cache hits — we'll run an Optimize review to quantify potential savings and set a safe config for the pilot."
  Acceptance: Demonstrated per-embedding cost reduction >=30% in pilot.

- Scenario D — Model quality regression during rollout:
  Setup: Customer sees hallucination uptick after model upgrade.
  Decision: Roll back to previous pinned version; run canary evals tied to their prompts; open a quality ticket and schedule a joint troubleshooting call.
  Script: "We’ll pin the last known-good model and run a canary evaluation against your golden prompt set; if improvements fail, we’ll fast-track a rollback and root cause investigation."
  Acceptance: Canary evals show identical or improved metrics vs baseline within 48 hours.

Facilitator cues & teaching points:
- Fast language for tradeoffs (30s): latency vs. cost vs. quality vs. compliance; have 2 short talking points per axis ready.
- When to bring SC/SE: immediate if customer needs Private or significant contract changes.
- When to promise action vs. demo: promise a measurable pilot; demo only after pilot scope agreed.

Checklist for running a 45-minute proving-ground session:
- 5m: intro & rubric (what success looks like)
- 20m: 4x 5m micro-scenarios (same rep rotates roles)
- 10m: debrief — what language landed, what was fuzzy
- 10m: action mapping (who owns follow-ups, which collateral to update)

Measurement rubric (simple):
- Reps produce a one-line decision + one fallback (binary: yes/no)
- Reps use the four tradeoff axes in explanation (count: 0–4)
- Post-session confidence rating (1–5) and one sticky phrase they will use in the field

Pilot plan (12 reps):
- Target cohort: 8 sellers + 4 SEs across North America and EU
- Duration: 4 weeks (two 45-minute sessions per rep, spaced 2 weeks apart)
- Success signals: 75% of reps hit rubric >=3 and we capture 8 new scripts to fold into the sales crib deck
- Risks: scheduling friction, inconsistent facilitator quality, legal edge-case questions beyond scope

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need a short slide deck (6–8 slides) capturing 3 exemplar scenarios and the rubric — owner? Tomás volunteered to draft but bandwidth is tight.
- Create a quick evaluation form (Google Form) and a central spreadsheet for results.
- Decide whether to record sessions for internal coaching — get consent template from legal.
- Which existing playcards should be retired/merged after this pilot? Compile list.

Attachments to create (next actions):
- 6-slide facilitator deck (Tomás)
- Google Form + scoring sheet (Marcus)
- Pilot schedule + invite template (Lena)

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep scenarios short and human — include customer pains not technical jargon.
- Avoid promising roadmap items; focus on configurable levers we control (routing, caching, quantization).
- Capture at least one counterintuitive win story per session (e.g., small model + prompt engineering beats big model on latency-sensitive workflow).

End of doc.
